sources.title: Pickling
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Pickling; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1376488146; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=2259607&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: Pickling solutions are typically highly acidic, with a pH of 4.6 or lower,[1] and high in salt, preventing enzymes from working and micro-organisms from multiplying.[2] Pickling can preserve perishable foods for months, or in some cases years.[3] Antimicrobial herbs and spices, such as mustard seed, garlic, cinnamon or cloves, are often added.[4] If the food contains sufficient moisture, a pickling brine may be produced simply by adding dry salt. For example, sour cabbage, sauerkraut, and kimchi are produced by salting the vegetables to draw out excess water. Natural fermentation at room temperature, by lactic acid bacteria, produces the required acidity. Other pickles are made by placing vegetables in vinegar. Unlike the canning process, pickling (which includes fermentation) does not require that the food be completely sterile. The acidity or salinity of the solution, the temperature of fermentation, and the exclusion of oxygen determine which microorganisms dominate, and determine the flavor of the end product.[5]

sources.title: Food drying
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Food drying; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1375576160; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=158573&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: Food drying is a method of food preservation in which food is dried (dehydrated or desiccated). Drying inhibits the growth of bacteria, yeasts, and mold through the removal of water. Dehydration has been used widely for this purpose since ancient times; the earliest known practice is 12,000 B.C. by inhabitants of the modern Asian and Middle Eastern regions.[2] Water is traditionally removed through evaporation by using methods such as air drying, sun drying, smoking or wind drying, although today electric food dehydrators or freeze-drying can be used to speed the drying process and ensure more consistent results.[3]

sources.title: Mulch
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Mulch; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1376736622; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=432174&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: A mulch is a layer of material applied to the surface of soil. Reasons for applying mulch include conservation of soil moisture, improving fertility and health of the soil, reducing weed growth, and enhancing the visual appeal of the area.

sources.title: Crop rotation
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Crop rotation; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1347627161; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=46470&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: Crop rotation is the practice of growing a series of different types of crops in the same area across a sequence of growing seasons. This practice reduces the reliance of crops on one set of nutrients, pest and weed pressure, along with the probability of developing resistant pests and weeds.

sources.title: Compiler
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Compiler; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1373605841; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=5739&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: There are many different types of compilers which produce output in different useful forms. A cross-compiler produces code for a different central processing unit (CPU) or operating system than the one on which the cross-compiler itself runs. A bootstrap compiler is often a temporary compiler, used for compiling a more permanent or better optimized compiler for a language.

sources.title: Assembly language
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Assembly language; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1376923639; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=1368&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: In computing, assembly language (alternatively assembler language[1] or symbolic machine code),[2][3][4] often referred to simply as assembly and commonly abbreviated as ASM or asm, is any low-level programming language with a very strong correspondence between the instructions in the language and the architecture's machine code instructions.[5] Assembly language usually has one statement per machine code instruction (1:1), but constants, comments, assembler directives,[6] symbolic labels of, e.g., memory locations, registers, and macros[7][1] are generally also supported.

sources.title: Constitution
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Constitution; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1377322873; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=5253&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: A constitution, or supreme law, is the aggregate of fundamental principles or established precedents that constitute the legal basis of a polity, organization or other type of entity, and commonly determines how that entity is to be governed.[1]

sources.title: Constitutional monarchy
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Constitutional monarchy; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1375076140; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=5649&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: Constitutional monarchy, also known as limited monarchy, parliamentary monarchy or democratic monarchy, is a form of monarchy in which the monarch exercises their authority in accordance with a constitution and is not alone in making decisions.[1][2][3][4] Constitutional monarchies differ from absolute monarchies (in which a monarch is the only decision-maker) in that they are bound to exercise powers and authorities within limits prescribed by an established legal framework. The monarch is frequently perceived as a visible symbol of national unity.[5]

sources.title: Absolute value
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Absolute value; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1371476443; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=991&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: In mathematics, the absolute value or modulus of a real number [TeX: {\displaystyle x}] , denoted [TeX: {\displaystyle |x|}] , is the (non-negative) magnitude of [TeX: {\displaystyle x}] measured without regard to its sign. Namely, [TeX: {\displaystyle |x|=x}] if [TeX: {\displaystyle x}] is a positive number, and [TeX: {\displaystyle |x|=-x}] if [TeX: {\displaystyle x}] is negative (in which case [TeX: {\displaystyle -x}] is positive), and [TeX: {\displaystyle |0|=0}] . For example, the absolute value of 3 is 3, and the absolute value of −3 is also 3. The absolute value of a number may be thought of as its distance from zero.

sources.title: Complex number
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Complex number; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1376162849; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=5826&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: In mathematics, a complex number is a number of the form ⁠ [TeX: {\displaystyle a+bi}] ⁠, where a and b are real numbers, and i is the imaginary unit, a number that satisfies the equation ⁠ [TeX: {\displaystyle \textstyle i^{2}=-1}] ⁠; the number a is called the real part of ⁠ [TeX: {\displaystyle a+bi}] ⁠, and b is called the imaginary part.

sources.title: Building insulation
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Building insulation; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1375683714; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=6900318&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: Building insulation is material used in a building (specifically the building envelope) to reduce the flow of thermal energy. While the majority of insulation in buildings is for thermal purposes, the term also applies to acoustic insulation, fire insulation, and impact insulation (e.g. for vibrations caused by industrial applications). Often an insulation material will be chosen for its ability to perform several of these functions at once.

sources.title: Passive ventilation
sources.license: Wikipedia contributors; Passive ventilation; https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=1356101732; contributor history https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?curid=7655739&action=history; CC BY-SA 4.0; selected transformed text distributed on the same terms; no added restrictions; https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/
sources.text: Passive ventilation is the process of supplying air to and removing air from an indoor space without using mechanical systems. It refers to the flow of external air to an indoor space as a result of pressure differences arising from natural forces.
